sanskrit_shloka:
अष्टावक्र उवाच ॥
तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति ।
किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृह्णाति किञ्चिद्धृष्यति कुप्यति ॥ ८-१॥
translation: Aṣṭāvakra said: Bondage is when the mind desires something, grieves over something, relinquishes something, grasps something, rejoices in something, or becomes angry.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Aṣṭāvakra said: Bondage is when the mind desires something, grieves over something, relinquishes something, grasps something, rejoices in something, or becomes angry.

commentary_faqs.question: How does Ashtavakra define bondage in this chapter?
commentary_faqs.answer: Ashtavakra defines bondage as any movement of the mind that involves desiring, grieving, renouncing, grasping, rejoicing, or feeling anger.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the relationship between the 'I' and liberation?
commentary_faqs.answer: According to Verse 4, liberation exists only when there is no 'I' (ego); the presence of the sense of a separate self is the very definition of bondage.

commentary_faqs.question: Why should one neither grasp nor renounce?
commentary_faqs.answer: Both grasping and renouncing are activities of the ego. True liberation is a state of effortless being that transcends the need to either hold onto or push away the world.

sanskrit_shloka:
तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति ।
न मुञ्चति न गृह्णाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥ ८-२॥
translation: Liberation is when the mind does not desire, does not grieve, does not relinquish, does not grasp, does not rejoice, and does not become angry.

sanskrit_shloka:
तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं सक्तं कास्वपि दृष्टिषु ।
तदा मोक्षो यदा चित्तमसक्तं सर्वदृष्टिषु ॥ ८-३॥
translation: Bondage is when the mind clings to any view; liberation is when the mind is unattached to all views.

sanskrit_shloka:
यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा ।
मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥ ८-४॥
translation: When there is no “I,” there is liberation; when there is “I,” there is bondage. Knowing this, lightly, grasp nothing and renounce nothing.
